title: Monetary Policy Report - November 2026
key_claim: CPI inflation is projected to rise to around 5% in 2027 Q2, averaging 4.9% that quarter; the MPC raised Bank Rate by 0.25 points to 4%; private sector regular pay growth is around 3% while surveys suggest about 4%.
frame_summary: Argues that an energy-driven rise in inflation now justifies tighter policy, with the risk that it passes into wages and prices the key judgement for 2027.

title: Monetary Policy Summary and minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee meeting ending on 4 November 2026
key_claim: The MPC voted 8-1 to raise Bank Rate to 4%; members saw a risk that wage settlements would turn out higher than firms expect, and that household attention to energy and food prices may be reflected in 2027 wage demands.
frame_summary: Frames the 2027 pay round as the test of whether the energy shock becomes persistent inflation, with the risk of second-round effects rising.
verbatim_quote: Households are particularly attentive to energy and food price inflation, which may be reflected in 2027 wage demands.
verbatim_list: there was a risk that outturns for wage settlements would turn out higher than firms’ current expectations

title: LPC advice to Government on 2027 minimum wage rates
key_claim: The LPC recommended a 3.9% National Living Wage increase to £13.21 from April 2027, short of the two-thirds-of-median reference point, judged above inflation forecasts for April 2027 to March 2028; employers report reaching the limit of costs they can absorb.
frame_summary: Argues for a cautious floor rise that protects real value over the year while respecting employers' cumulative cost pressures in a low-hire labour market.

verbatim_list: Many are concerned that they have reached the limits of the costs that they can absorb

title: Labour Market Outlook - autumn 2026
key_claim: The median expected basic pay increase remains 3% across all sectors while inflation is expected to peak around 5% in the first half of 2027; real pay is currently 0.8%; the net employment balance is +10 for a seventh subdued quarter.
frame_summary: Describes employers holding pay expectations flat and hiring subdued even as inflation climbs, under pressure from costs and employment law reform.

title: Pay trends 2026 | October Report
key_claim: The median award was 3.1% in the three months to September 2026; most awards matched or fell below last year's; employers forecast a 3% median for the year to 31 August 2027; the 4.8% Real Living Wage rise exceeds both.
frame_summary: Reads UK pay settlements as stable and tightly clustered at about 3%, constrained by affordability and employer National Insurance, with little sign of acceleration.

title: Low pay has stopped falling for the first time in 15 years
key_claim: The share of employees in low pay rose slightly to 2.8% in April 2026, the first time in 15 years it has not fallen, because the minimum wage has moved to a 'hold steady' phase.
frame_summary: Argues the minimum wage has stopped pulling the low-paid up relative to the median, so further gains for low earners now depend on policy choice rather than momentum.
verbatim_quote: a ‘hold steady’ phase after years of being ramped up

title: UK hiring intentions remain near record lows, CIPD finds
key_claim: Only 58% of private sector organisations plan to recruit over the next three months; the CIPD said rising inflation and further Employment Rights Act reforms add to employer pressures.
frame_summary: Reports the CIPD survey as evidence of a frozen hiring market in which employers face rising costs from inflation and employment law at once.

frame_summary: Reports settlements edging up but expected to lag inflation in 2027, with cost pressures limiting what employers can offer.
